sources.title: Rivian - Charging (Canada/North America page)
sources.notes: States: all 2026+ Rivian vehicles have a built-in NACS charge port; 2022-2025 have CCS and need a NACS DC adapter for Tesla Superchargers; battery warmed/cooled by preconditioning; every R2 has NACS. Page is in km (Canadian locale) and says Superchargers across North America.

sources.title: InsideEVs - Rivian R1T/R1S Charging Power Peaks At 210 kW
sources.notes: Quotes EPA paperwork: DC fast charging peaks at 210 kW; 11.5 kW onboard charger; about 135 kWh pack (9 modules, 7,776 2170 cells, Samsung SDI); voltage 216-459 V. Relays maker figures filed with EPA (Gen 1).

sources.title: InsideEVs - Second-gen Rivian R1 debut
sources.notes: Gen 1 pack ratings: Standard 105.9, Standard+ 121 (NMC), Large 135, Max 149 kWh; Gen 2 Standard 92.5 kWh LFP (leaked certification documents).

sources.title: Green Car Reports - 2025 Rivian R1T/R1S LFP review
sources.notes: Gen 2 usable: Standard 92.5 (LFP), Large 109.4 (NCA, 2170), Max 141.5 kWh (NCA); peak 220 kW on Large and Max, 200 kW on Standard; 10-80 % in 30-41 min depending on pack.

sources.title: autoevolution - Choosing the ideal 2025 Rivian R1S or R1T battery pack
sources.notes: Gen 2 table: Standard 92.5 LFP 200 kW; Large 109.4 NMC 220 kW; Max 141.5 NMC 220 kW. Earlier Large 50G NCA cells; Max 53G NCA (gross 149).

sources.title: autoevolution - 2027 Rivian R1S and R1T revealed in EPA certification documents
sources.notes: 2027: Premium 105.5 kWh (formerly Large), Premium Long Range 140 kWh (formerly Max); Performance (tri) and Quad only with 140 kWh; Standard gone. No charging figures.

sources.title: InsideEVs - Rivian is adding a key charging feature to the R1S and R1T (software 2025.18)
sources.notes: Manual battery preconditioning for DC fast charging added without navigation, Gen 1 and Gen 2; navigation-triggered preconditioning existed before. Gen 2 Large peak rate raised to 215 kW.

sources.title: Wikipedia - Rivian R1T
sources.notes: Max pack later revised to 142 kWh usable; 105/121/135/149 kWh packs; AC 11.52 kW at 240 V (48 A).

sources.title: Electrek - Rivian R2 EPA numbers out: 217 kW DC charge, up to 335 mi
sources.notes: R2 seems capable of a peak DC rate of 217 kW (from EPA data); 10-80 % about 29 min (Rivian); NACS connector.

sources.title: Battery Design - Rivian R2 pack 2026 update
sources.notes: R2: total 94 kWh, net 87.9 kWh (cited to Rivian engineers; EPA-certified usable 86.8), NCMA 4695 LG cells (reverse-engineered), nominal 353 V, peak 230 kW / 630 A, 10-80 % 29 min.

sources.title: The Drive - Rivian goes all in on the R2
sources.notes: 87.9 kWh pack on Performance, Premium and Standard Long Range; 10-80 % in 29 min; NACS port, Supercharger capable.

sources.title: InsideEVs - Rivian R2 charging test
sources.notes: Peaked at 229 kW; Rivian stuck with a 400 V battery architecture for the R2.

sources.title: Lucid - Charging your Lucid Air
sources.notes: Manual Start Preconditioning plus Smart Preconditioning (automatic when routing to a fast charger in Lucid Navigation); J1772 (CCS1) port; Tesla Superchargers (V3+) with a Lucid-approved NACS-to-CCS1 adapter.

sources.title: Lucid Canada - Charging your Lucid Air

sources.title: InsideEVs - Lucid Air Dream Edition: 118 kWh is the usable battery capacity
sources.notes: Lucid confirmed to InsideEVs that 118 kWh is both usable and total for the Dream Edition; Grand Touring 112 kWh listed as usable; >900 V; up to around 300 kW.

sources.title: ArenaEV - Lucid Air Grand Touring Performance (2022) specs

sources.title: Evercars - 2026 Lucid Air trim comparison

sources.title: Electrek - Lucid launches 2026 Air lineup
sources.notes: Touring DC charging peak remains 250 kW; denser cells raise Touring range to 431 mi; from 31 July 2025 every Air can use Tesla V3+ Superchargers with the $220 adapter.

sources.title: Lucid - Charging your Lucid Gravity
sources.notes: Native NACS port (AC and DC); AC up to 19.2 kW (80 A); Smart (navigation) and manual battery preconditioning; V3/V4 Superchargers with Plug & Charge; up to 220 kW at Superchargers; 200 miles in 10.5 min on a 400 kW charger.

sources.title: Wards - 2025 Lucid Gravity: 450 miles of range and NACS port

sources.title: KBB - 2026 Lucid Gravity specs
